```markdown
# lock-closures roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: none.
Choices made: none.

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | How the chance that a lock closes moves with the upstream river-gauge level | A | 1 | measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | A 7-day closure-risk outlook for each lock from the river-level forecast | A | 2 | one model run a day, small once O1's model exists; basis: Stage 1's measured fit time |
| O3 | Separate closure curves for all 14 locks, pooled across locks | A | 3 | about 14× Stage 1's data; basis: Stage 1's measured data volume |
| O4 | A closure-history map for the canal's boat operators | A | 4 | about a day of work; basis: one static map page |

Tracks: A — closure study (research).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Closure chance against upstream gauge level
      Objective: Estimate how the chance of a lock closure moves with the upstream river-gauge level, on real closure records and real gauge readings.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing (the repository holds only an empty `lock_closures` package and an import smoke test)
      Produces: a fitted closure-probability-vs-gauge-level relationship, with the loaded closure and gauge data it was fit on, reusable by O2 and O3; specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — a closure-probability curve against upstream gauge level, with its uncertainty, produced from real records and reported in the findings file; the findings file records the measured cost of the real run: data volume loaded, load time and fit time.
      Leaves out: traceability from each estimate back to its gauge readings → Ranked-list item "Traceability"; per-lock curves → O3; forecast inputs, forecast-vintage (point-in-time) handling and daily scheduling → O2; operator-facing map → O4
      ROUTING: brainstorming

## Ranked list — Track A

1. O2 — one model run a day, small once O1's model exists; basis: Stage 1's measured fit time. Picks up forecast-vintage (point-in-time) handling and daily scheduling.
2. O3 — about 14× Stage 1's data; basis: Stage 1's measured data volume.
3. O4 — about a day of work; basis: one static map page.
4. Traceability — each closure estimate names the gauge readings it came from (the board will ask). Not ranked by partner; placed last provisionally, to be ranked at the first re-rank. Cost: measured once Stage 1's data shape is known.

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, which writing-plans copies
verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick
> the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every committed stage is ticked and no Ranked list waits, re-run the gap
rubric over the Outcomes list (O1–O4), with evidence per verdict (implementing
stage/plan, Deviation notes, deferred_items entries). Ranked-list items never
promoted have parked to `specs/deferred_items.md`. Unmet outcomes exit by a
new stage or a written deferral.
```

---

Roadmap written to `specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md` and committed on `main`.

**Partition.** One research track, so only the core stage is committed: **Stage 1 (O1)**, run on real closure records and gauge readings, with its findings file recording the result and the measured cost (data volume, load time, fit time). O2, O3 and O4 wait in the Ranked list in your order. Once Stage 1 has run, a resume reports its finding and cost, and asks you which item to promote next. The order follows your ranking. O1 is also the dependency for O2 and O3, so ranking and dependency agree.

**Traceability.** The board's question, "which gauge readings did each estimate come from?", is a quality the study needs eventually but doesn't need to work. I've kept it out of Stage 1's Exit and made it its own Ranked-list item. You didn't rank it, so I put it last provisionally. Tell me if it should sit higher, for example before O2 if the board sees outlooks first.

**One thing I should have raised before you confirmed the track.** O4, the operators' map, serves a different use from the study and doesn't need O1's answer. Inside the research track, it waits behind Stage 1 and every re-rank. I recommend splitting it into its own known-progression Track B with a single stage, so it can be built whenever you like. Since you ranked it last, keeping it where it is also works. Say which you prefer.

**Approval.** Please approve the partition, with or without the two changes above. On approval:

Next: /clear (or a fresh session), then brainstorming on Stage 1 of `specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md`. The stage spec's Rollout note carries:

`Roadmap: specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md, Stage 1`
